report.summary: Chunk 3 of _PyNaming definitions: _py_dotted, _disambiguate, _View, _PyNaming class with docstring.

handoff.purpose: Define dotted name utilities and _PyNaming class with multi-center view logic.

symbols.name: _py_dotted
symbols.note: Converts a relative file path to a dotted module name by stripping .py suffix or last extension, replacing '/' with '.'.

symbols.name: _STUB_SUFFIXES
symbols.note: Tuple of stub file suffixes, currently only '.pyi'.

symbols.name: _disambiguate
symbols.note: Returns the one real source file from a list of candidates, or None if ambiguous. Prefers non-stub if exactly one real source exists.

symbols.name: _View
symbols.note: NamedTuple representing one importer's view of the Python dotted namespace, with tops, known, rel_by_dotted, and canon fields.

symbols.name: _PyNaming
symbols.note: Class for Python dotted-name tables resolved from the importer's point of view, with multi-center support and alias handling.

claims.text: A ``.pyi`` is a type stub DECLARING the module its ``.py`` sibling defines -- not a second module. Both strip to one dotted name, which is why the naming table has to say which file that name binds to.
claims.why: The code defines _STUB_SUFFIXES = (".pyi",) and _disambiguate treats .pyi files as stubs, preferring non-.pyi files when exactly one real source exists.

claims.text: Order-independent by construction: the answer is a function of the SET of candidates, never of the order they were walked in.
claims.why: The function iterates over the list only to filter real sources; the logic does not depend on order. It returns the single real source if exactly one exists, else None.

claims.text: The previous ``{_py_dotted(rel): rel for ...}`` dict comprehension was a last-writer-wins race decided by ``os.walk`` -- measured at 141 live collisions on project_tct, every one a .py/.pyi pair, and it bound the name to the STUB.
claims.why: This refers to previous implementation and external data (project_tct) not present in this chunk.

claims.text: 1. A stub is not a rival. If exactly one candidate is real source, the name is that module and the stub is its declaration. This is a precedence rule about what a ``.pyi`` MEANS, not a tie-break.
claims.why: The function returns the single real source when there is exactly one non-.pyi file among candidates.

claims.text: 2. Otherwise refuse. Two genuine modules claiming one dotted name is a real ambiguity, and a wrong edge lies about what depends on what -- strictly worse than a missing one. Callers report the refusal with counts rather than binding to whichever file sorted first.
claims.why: When there is not exactly one real source (0 or >1), the function returns None, refusing to bind. The docstring mentions callers report counts, but that is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A declared ``center`` means "this subtree IS the project", so it is also the PACKAGE ROOT: ``TCT_app/controller/danger_gate.py`` is run with ``TCT_app`` on ``sys.path`` and its siblings therefore write ``from controller.danger_gate import ...``. Naming it ``TCT_app.controller.danger_gate`` (the repo-root form) matched nothing, and ``resolve_python_imports`` dropped the edge before it ever reached the ``known`` lookup. 87% of project_tct's map was isolated for this one reason.
claims.why: The claim refers to center configuration, resolve_python_imports, and project_tct data not present in this chunk.

claims.text: The obvious fix -- strip the prefix and let ``internal_tops`` grow -- is unsafe, and the danger is on the *other* side of the membership test. ``internal_tops`` is the eligibility gate, and two of its three uses in ``parse.py`` (the plain ``import x`` branch, and the fallback) admit a name with NO ``known`` check at all. Stripping ``TCT_app/`` globally would inject ``controller``, ``devices``, ``gui``, ``data`` -- generic names that collide with real PyPI and vendored packages -- into a table consulted by every file in the repo. project_tct carries 8516 shell import records today that are inert only because no shell file's top segment can equal ``TCT_app``; widen the global table and any vendored file writing ``import data`` becomes eligible to bind onto a center file. That would manufacture false edges, which is the one outcome worse than the missing ones we are fixing.
claims.why: The claim references internal_tops, parse.py, shell import records, and project_tct data not present in this chunk.

claims.text: So the table is selected by the importer: * a file under center C sees C's files by their PACKAGE-RELATIVE name, and everything else in the repo by its repo-root name; * a file under no center sees the repo-root table, unchanged, which is byte-for-byte what every file saw before this change. Shell eligibility therefore cannot move, and a repo with no center declared gets exactly one view that is identical to the old global one.
claims.why: The claim describes behavior of view selection and shell eligibility, which is not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: A view strips only its OWN center, which dissolves the multi-center collision case rather than having to arbitrate it: with ``center=["a","b"]`` both containing ``controller/``, inside a's view ``controller.x`` is a's file and b's is still ``b.controller.x`` -- which is exactly what the runtime does, since ``a`` runs with ``a`` on sys.path and not ``b``. The collision that stripping DOES create is against the shell: a center file whose stripped name matches a repo-root module (``a/controller/x.py`` vs ``controller/x.py``). That one is a genuine ambiguity and is refused, not guessed -- see ``_disambiguate``.
claims.why: The claim describes multi-center view behavior and collision handling, which is not implemented in this chunk. It references _disambiguate, which is present but its behavior in this context is not shown.

claims.text: A center can sit at either of two places in a real layout, and the config cannot tell us which: * the center IS the sys.path root (project_tct: ``TCT_app`` is the cwd, so its files write ``from controller.danger_gate import ...``); * the center is a PACKAGE on the parent path (the repo root is on sys.path, so its files write ``from TCT_app import core``). Both spellings name the same file, so accepting both is not a guess and costs no precision. What we refuse is two IDENTITIES for one file: the repo-root spelling is registered as an ALIAS in this view's lookup tables, and every resolved target is canonicalised back to the package-relative name before it reaches ``dep_edges``. So ``fan_in`` -- accumulated over ``dep_edges`` keys -- still counts each file exactly once, and the top fan-in table cannot shift for a bookkeeping reason.
claims.why: The claim describes alias registration and canonicalization, which is not implemented in this chunk. It references dep_edges and fan_in not present here.

claims.text: The alias lives ONLY in its own center's view, and it is that center's own path prefix, so it cannot widen what a shell file is eligible to bind. An alias also never displaces a real module: if some file genuinely owns that spelling in this view, the alias is dropped.
claims.why: The claim describes alias scoping and displacement behavior, which is not implemented in this chunk.

observations.what: _disambiguate returns None when there are zero or multiple real sources.
_View is a NamedTuple with four fields: tops, known, rel_by_dotted, canon.
_PyNaming docstring is extensive but contains many claims about behavior not implemented in this chunk.
